manual.assorteddecor.chapter.building_bl: The lumber mill cuts a plank into four beams, and the stonecutter an iron ingot into an iron beam. They run along the top or bottom of the block, the way you are facing. A beam placed against the side of another grows an arm to meet it, so they cross and tee on their own.
Brick blocks are cut into basketweave and herringbone patterns on the stonecutter.
Cobblestone can be reinforced with iron or framed in sticks, and calcite and cobbled deepslate together make a checkerboard.

Fluted stone and columns come off the stonecutter from any of the stones.

Columns have a base at the bottom, a capital at the top and a plain shaft between. They can also be placed against a wall to lay them on their side.

Almost every block here comes off a stonecutter or lumber mill. Stone and metal are cut on the stonecutter, wood on the lumber mill. Most come as slabs and stairs too, and the bricks and tiles as walls.
Obsidian is cut into polished obsidian, and lapis and redstone blocks into bricks, tiles and polished blocks.
Glowstone cut into bricks on the stonecutter.
The stonecutter's twin for wood. Put in planks and pick what to cut them into. It also supports logs to break up into any of the child blocks and items.
Nine porkchops pressed around a bone. It comes apart into the nine porkchopsagain.
Iron, gold and diamond blocks are cut into bricks on the stonecutter, one for one.
The lumber mill cuts a plank into eight panels. A panel lines the face you place it against. It can be placed against a wall, a floor or a ceiling.

Every stone is cut into bricks, tiles and a carved creeper face. Stone, granite, diorite, andesite, calcite, tuff, dripstone, deepslate, blackstone, sandstone and red sandstone.

The stonecutter makes them from the raw stone or from its polished form.
The lumber mill cuts every kind of planks into parquet and framed planks.
Every stone's bricks have a mossy and a cracked form, made the way vanilla stone bricks are. Vines or moss for mossy, a furnace for cracked.
manual.assorteddecor.chapter.colorizer.b:
A colorized block can only be set by being brushed with the Colorizer Brush.

Shift right click a supported full block and the brush will take the blocks texture. Then right click with the brush on a Colorizer and see it get applied.
The panel, beam and column from building blocks, cut from a colorizer on the stonecutter. They behave just as the wooden and stone ones do.
manual.assorteddecor.chapter.colorizer.c:
A colorizer is a blank block that borrows another block's texture.

Everything in this chapter and the two after it is built from colorizers, which is why a chair, a slope and a fireplace can all match the wall behind them.
manual.assorteddecor.chapter.colorizer.d: A colorized door wearing the same block as the wall around it is a hidden entrance, and a colorized trap door does the same for a floor.
manual.assorteddecor.chapter.colorizer.p: A pyramid takes up half a block, and a large pyramid takes a full one and can be climbed, with its high point in the middle.
manual.assorteddecor.chapter.colorizer.s: Slabs, vertical slabs, stairs, walls, fences and fence gates, all colorizable.

Slopes are the angled half of the set. A slope is half a block cut corner to corner and walks like straight stairs; a sloped angle can only be walked up on the point it faces.

Sloped intersections act as corner stairs, oblique slopes fill the corner a staircase leaves, slanted corners are a steeper climb, and sloped posts cannot be climbed at all. Corners are a sideways cut of a full block.

All of them can be flipped upside down as you place them, the way a slab is.
manual.assorteddecor.chapter.decorations: A bone decoration needs no firing. Place it and right click to cycle through the shapes.
A cage displays whatever you put in it, turning slowly. Use it with a Pokeball from Assorted Tools to show the caught monster.

Clay decorations are crafted unfired and have to go through a furnace before they are any use.

Once placed, right click to cycle through the options.

A copper case weathers where it stands, through exposed, weathered and oxidized, like any other copper. What is on show stays on show through every step.

An axe scrapes a stage back off it, and a honeycomb waxes it to hold the stage it is at. Only the plain copper case is crafted.

A display case can hold 1, 4, or 9 items depending on the size setup in the display.

Right clicking on a position allows you to place an item in that spot. Use the Resizing Tool to change the size of the case.

Wooden, stone, copper, iron, gold and diamond cases differ only in the colour of their frame.
A fountain block pushes water up out of itself, for a courtyard that needed a middle.

The museum edition stands two blocks tall. A carpeted plinth with the glass case on top of it. Everything goes in the glass half.

The plinth carries a placard. Name the case on an anvil before you place it, or right click the plinth with a named name tag.

A planter pot is crafted unfired and has to go through a furnace before it will hold anything.

Once placed, right click to cycle through the filling material. The pot supports whichever plants suit the filling material it is set to.

A case is placed showing one item on one shelf, and that one item is drawn large. Use the resizing tool on it to grow it to four items on two shelves, again for nine on three, and once more to come back to one.

Shrinking a case hands back whatever it can no longer show.
Siding boards a wall in horizontal or vertical planking, in any of the sixteen colors. The color comes from the paint roller in the recipe.
Decorative stone and stone paths both come off the stonecutter from plain stone, which makes them cheap enough to use by the wall.
manual.assorteddecor.chapter.doors.chain: Chain link makes a fence you can see through
manual.assorteddecor.chapter.doors.doors: Glass, quartz and steel doors, for the places a plank door looks wrong. All three can take a padlock from Assorted Storage like any other door.
manual.assorteddecor.chapter.fires.chimn: A chimney on a lit fireplace smokes. They stack, so the smoke can be carried up through a roof.
manual.assorteddecor.chapter.fires.firep: A firepit is the outdoor version, lit with flint and steel and put out with a punch. The covered one has a net over it.

Light a fireplace with flint and steel and it burns and gives light. Punch it to put it out.

Fireplaces placed side by side move their corner posts out of each other's way, so a row reads as one wide hearth.
manual.assorteddecor.chapter.fires.firer: A fire ring is a ring of stones around a fire, lit and put out like the rest. Good for ghost stories.
manual.assorteddecor.chapter.fires.stove: A stove lights and goes out the same way a fireplace does, and takes a chimney on top.
manual.assorteddecor.chapter.furniture.l: A lamp post builds itself three blocks high from the one you place. And the top gives light.
manual.assorteddecor.chapter.furniture.s: Chairs turn to face the way you place them. Stools are the shorter version, and a planter pot sits on stool nicely.
manual.assorteddecor.chapter.furniture.t:
Tables placed next to each other work out where their legs belong, so a long table has room underneath it.

A counter is a table without the legs, for running along a wall.
manual.assorteddecor.chapter.gates.castl:
Place a castle gate against the underside of a solid block and it drops all the way down to the ground. Gates side by side and facing the same way will open and close as one.

Blow the gate trumpet to open it up from afar.

Redstone at the top block holds it open while it is powered.
manual.assorteddecor.chapter.gates.garag: A garage door hangs and fills down the same way a castle gate does, as a solid panel rather than bars. The garage remote opens and closes it, and redstone works on it too.
manual.assorteddecor.chapter.hanging.cal: A calendar on the wall keeps count of the days you have been in the world.
manual.assorteddecor.chapter.hanging.clo: A wall clock shows the time of day.
manual.assorteddecor.chapter.hanging.fra: Right click a hung frame with a dye and it takes that color, so a wall can be framed in one shade or in several.

Frames add depth where wallpaper adds pattern, in wood or iron, and right click to cycle through their patterns the same way.

A frame is sturdier than wallpaper: take the block out from behind it and it stays where it is.
manual.assorteddecor.chapter.hanging.neo: A neon sign works like an ordinary sign, except colored text glows and there is a proper editor for getting the layout right. Three backgrounds to choose from.
manual.assorteddecor.chapter.hanging.wal:
Wallpaper covers a wall without taking up the block. Once it is up, right click to cycle through the designs, and right click with a dye to color it.

Wallpaper next to wallpaper tries to match its neighbours, so a whole wall lines up on its own.
manual.assorteddecor.chapter.lights.flur: Fluro blocks are bright, flat and come in all sixteen colors.
manual.assorteddecor.chapter.lights.illu: Illumination tubes and plates light a room the way a torch does, but go on any face of a block and sit flush against it.
manual.assorteddecor.chapter.lights.lant: Bone, iron and paper lanterns, for when a torch is the wrong look for the room.
manual.assorteddecor.chapter.roads.aspha: Tarballs make asphalt, and asphalt is what every road block here is built from.
manual.assorteddecor.chapter.roads.roadw:
Roadway is asphalt laid flat.

It comes in all sixteen colors for markings, plus a lit version and a manhole, so a road can be striped like a real one.
manual.assorteddecor.chapter.roads.rolle:
A paint roller loaded with a dye is how road markings and siding get their color. Use it on wool, carpet, concrete or concrete powder to recolor it as well.

There is a roller for every color.
manual.assorteddecor.chapter.roads.sidew: Sidewalk allow you to walk faster than you otherwise would and paths just look nice. 🙂
manual.assorteddecor.chapter.roads.stone: A stone path is the quieter surface for a garden, cut from plain stone on the stonecutter.
manual.assorteddecor.description: Blocks that take on the look of other blocks, plus furniture, lights, decorations, wall art, roads and more.
manual.assorteddecor.title: Assorted Decor
tooltip.resizing_tool: Use on a display case to adjust the display size
